hook.line: Altamira sends Hernando a note the night before the building work starts under his window. He is not grateful, and he says so in the politest words he knows.
hook.en: How thoughtful of you to warn me so far in advance!

examples.es:
Te aviso hoy que mañana empiezan las obras.
¡Qué detalle avisarme con tanta anticipación!
examples.en:
I'm telling you today that the building work starts tomorrow.
How thoughtful of you to warn me so far in advance!

examples.es:
Rompí dos tazas mientras ayudaba.
Gracias por tu ayuda, no sé qué habría hecho sin ti.
examples.en:
I broke two cups while helping.
Thanks for your help, I don't know what I'd have done without you.

examples.es:
Nos cortaron el agua el día de la inauguración.
¡Qué detalle!
examples.en:
They cut off our water on opening day.
How thoughtful!

examples.es:
Me trajiste un tinto cuando llegué.
¡Qué detalle! Gracias.
examples.en:
You brought me a coffee when I arrived.
How thoughtful! Thanks.

examples.es:
Llegaste una hora tarde.
Gracias por tanta puntualidad.
examples.en:
You arrived an hour late.
Thanks for being so punctual.

examples.es:
Pagué cuatro millones por el carro y no arranca.
¡Tremendo negocio!
examples.en:
I paid four million for the car and it won't start.
What a deal!

rule: Sometimes the words are warm and the facts say otherwise. *¡Qué detalle!* means how thoughtful, but after bad news it means the opposite. Nothing marks it on the page: if every word makes sense and the sentence clashes with what just happened, assume irony. Among friends it is affectionate teasing; with a boss it has teeth. After a real kindness the same words are sincere (the tinto), so always check what came before. English does it too (*thanks a lot*), and Spanish loves doing it with very polite phrases.
smallPrint: Teachers call this verbal irony: saying the opposite of what you mean.

readAndPick.es:
Nos cortaron el agua el día de la inauguración.
¡Qué detalle!

Me trajiste un tinto cuando llegué.
¡Qué detalle!

Llegaste una hora tarde.
Gracias por tanta puntualidad.
options: The speaker is annoyed and being sarcastic.
The speaker is praising someone who was on time.

readAndPick.es:
Rompí dos tazas mientras ayudaba.
Gracias por tu ayuda, no sé qué habría hecho sin ti.
options: The speaker is thankful for the help.
The speaker is not thankful at all.
The speaker is asking for more help.

readAndPick.es:

options: The speaker got a great deal.
The speaker is joking about a bad deal.

yourTurn.prompt: Your friend brought you a tinto when you arrived, and you mean it. Choose *¡Qué detalle!* or *¡Qué desastre!* and type the sincere reaction.
yourTurn.why: *¡Qué detalle!* is how thoughtful, and here nothing clashes.

yourTurn.prompt: A friend warned you the night before the building work started. Say it ironically: How thoughtful of you to warn me so far in advance!
accept: Qué detalle avisarme con tanta anticipación
yourTurn.why: The warm words clash with the bad timing, and that is the irony.

yourTurn.prompt: You broke two cups while helping. Your friend says ironically: Thanks for your help, I don't know what I'd have done without you.
yourTurn.answer: Gracias por tu ayuda, no sé qué habría hecho sin ti.
accept: Gracias por tu ayuda. No sé qué habría hecho sin ti.
yourTurn.why: Over the top gratitude after a disaster signals sarcasm.

yourTurn.prompt: Your friend arrived an hour late. Say ironically (to a friend): Thanks for being so punctual.
yourTurn.why: Praising the opposite of what happened is the whole trick.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it polite (to one person, *usted*): *Gracias por tu ayuda, no sé qué habría hecho sin ti.*
yourTurn.answer: Gracias por su ayuda, no sé qué habría hecho sin usted.
accept: Gracias por su ayuda. No sé qué habría hecho sin usted.

yourTurn.prompt: Your car won't start after you paid four million for it. Say ironically: What a deal!
yourTurn.why: *Tremendo* is a big word for a bad deal, which makes it ironic.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about two friends (you all): *Gracias por tu ayuda, no sé qué habría hecho sin ti.*
yourTurn.answer: Gracias por su ayuda, no sé qué habría hecho sin ustedes.
accept: Gracias por su ayuda. No sé qué habría hecho sin ustedes.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *qué* in an exclamation, the noun comes without *un*.

pitfalls.wrong: No sé qué hice sin ti.
pitfalls.right: No sé qué habría hecho sin ti.
pitfalls.why: What I would have done is *habría hecho*, the would have form.

personal: Think of a small disaster this week. Write the ironic thanks you would give the person responsible, with *¡Qué detalle...!* or *Gracias por...*
